title: Geometric regularity criterion for smoothness over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if, for every finitely generated field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] and every point $x\in X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the local ring $\mathcal O_{X_L,x}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Here finitely generated means that $L$ is generated as a field over $k$ by finitely many elements; no perfectness, dimension, reducedness, connectedness or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), pointwise equivalence at every point; Tag 038T (definition-geometrically-regular), finitely generated field extensions
